transcript:
Meeting header: Date/Time: 2025-09-02 14:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Jamal Ortiz (Redwood SE); Laura Martinez (BrightCart, Head of ML); Evan Park (PM); Sahil Rao (Data Scientist)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. Quick roll call, then we'll jump into the quality eval results for this week.
[00:10] Laura Martinez: Hi, Laura here.
[00:12] Evan Park: Evan here.
[00:14] Sahil Rao: Sahil here.
[00:18] Jamal Ortiz: Jamal from Redwood.
[00:20] Maya Chen: Cool. Jamal, do you want to start with the topline on v3 prompt set?
[00:26] Jamal Ortiz: Yeah, sure. So we ran the v3 prompts against the pilot dataset, about 5,000 prompts in the baseline run. Overall pass rate is 82% on our rubric which is down about 4 points versus v2 — so we flagged that as a regression. The regression looks concentrated in the product-recommendation templates and some of the multi-turn carts.
[00:45] Laura Martinez: Hm, interesting. Is that across all scoring modes or more with the higher temperature runs?
[00:50] Jamal Ortiz: Mostly at the higher temperature (0.9) and also when we disabled reranking. When reranking is on with our scoring threshold at 0.65, the pass moves back up to 88%. So there's a strong signal that reranking plus a stricter threshold helps.
[01:10] Evan Park: Can you remind me quickly how the reranker is working? We use a tuned logistic model?
[01:15] Jamal Ortiz: Yes, it's our lightweight reranker — basically a featurized scoring model that reranks N-best and prefers safer and more on-brand outputs. It's not the full offline ranker, it's the inline one that runs at token-level cost. Sometimes in the transcript the name got munged but it's the Redwood reranker.
[01:32] Sahil Rao: Are we seeing new safety false positives? Last week we had an issue where the filter caught some benign promotional text.
[01:39] Jamal Ortiz: Good point. There are a couple of new false positives in the compliance guardrail for medical-sounding phrases in product descriptions. We think it's because the v3 prompts include longer context that triggers the safety model more often.
[01:52] Laura Martinez: That could be a problem for our catalog. We can't have legitimate product copy blocked. Can we tune the guardrail?
[01:58] Jamal Ortiz: Yeah, two levers: adjust the safety threshold and add a small allow-list for our domain terms. We can also move some checks to post-processing heuristics so they don't surface to end users.
[02:10] Maya Chen: Quick check: what's the latency impact when reranking is enabled? Evan, you asked about cost earlier.
[02:16] Jamal Ortiz: Reranking adds about 80-120ms p50 on hosted. With Dedicated it's cheaper in CPU/GPU terms but still ~60-90ms. There's a tradeoff — enabling prefix KV caching and smaller N-best sizes reduces latency. We showed microbenchmarks in the shared sheet (see link: https://redwood.link/brightcart-eval-2025).
[02:37] Evan Park: That latency looks fine for checkout flows, maybe less so for quick search autocomplete. Do we have a fallback policy?
[02:45] Jamal Ortiz: Yes: fallback to a lighter prompt variant plus no rerank for the autocomplete route. We can route by endpoint: low-latency route uses the faster model variant, high-quality route uses rerank and may hit Dedicated if you want consistent p99.
[02:58] Laura Martinez: About Dedicated — we discussed that with procurement. A question: if we go Dedicated, do logs still leave our VPC?
[03:05] Maya Chen: By default Dedicated keeps inference inside the reserved capacity and Redwood can optionally offer a private control plane (Private deployment). For Dedicated we offer options: bring-your-own-key (KMS) and audit logs forwarded to your SIEM. We have customers with strict residency keeping everything in VPC.
[03:20] Evan Park: Good. Back to the regression: Jamal, you mentioned the product-recommendation templates are the issue. Can you show an example?
[03:27] Jamal Ortiz: Sure. Example prompt id 4, prompt text: "User likes eco-friendly travel mugs, showing recommended items with complementary accessories". v2 output: concise product list with ratings. v3 output sometimes injected promotional verbs and a speculative phrase that the user might be allergic which triggered safety heuristics. Sounds like hallucination plus guardrail false positive.
[03:52] Sahil Rao: We saw that too. I have a few of those edge cases in the extra prompt set I uploaded.
[03:58] Maya Chen: Great — Sahil, can you share those two additional edge-case prompt sets by end of week? We'll add them to the extended eval.
[04:05] Sahil Rao: Yep, will do.
[04:08] Jamal Ortiz: For scoring, we propose tightening the pass threshold from 0.65 to 0.70 for these templates, and also enabling rerank at inference path. That recovers most of the loss without retraining.
[04:21] Laura Martinez: If we tighten threshold, do we risk more false negatives? We don't want legitimate answers downgraded.
[04:26] Jamal Ortiz: True. That's why we also want a domain allow-list and some post-filters. We'll produce a false positive / false negative breakdown in the extended eval.
[04:36] Evan Park: On the operational side, what's the cost delta with reranking on across our projected volume?
[04:42] Jamal Ortiz: With your projected 3M monthly tokens, reranking as configured adds roughly 12% to inference token cost in hosted mode. Dedicated would lower that to about ~6-7% relative increase because of amortized GPU cost. We'll put a detailed cost table in the follow-up sheet.
[04:58] Maya Chen: Also, just flagging that quantization profiles can help. If you run the service on q4_8 or q6, we can get lower cost with minimal quality loss on many of these templates.
[05:10] Sahil Rao: Any model variants you recommend?
[05:12] Jamal Ortiz: For BrightCart we recommend the redwood-xxl-1 (float16) for core catalog generation, and a smaller redwood-large-1 for autocomplete. If you're very cost-sensitive, try the quantized redwood-xxl-1-q4_0 variant. We'll include perf/quality tradeoffs in the spreadsheet.
[05:28] Laura Martinez: One operational ask: we need audit logs for every inference that hits the compliance guardrail. Can Redwood provide that?
[05:34] Maya Chen: Yes, we can forward structured audit events including prompt id, model variant, guardrail flag, and truncated user content. We have templates for SIEM ingestion. Those logs can be pushed to your S3 or Splunk.
[05:45] Evan Park: Good. A couple of nitty-gritty items from last week's notes — Maya, you were going to send the SOC2 summary and the security questionnaire.
[05:52] Maya Chen: I have a SOC2 excerpt ready; I'll attach it to the follow-up. Also we'll include the completed security questionnaire and the whitepaper on network topology for Dedicated/Private.
[06:03] Laura Martinez: Perfect.
[06:06] Jamal Ortiz: Back to the experimental results: we also ran a prompt paraphrase augmentation and that reduced hallucination by about 6 points but increased instruction-following errors in a small subset. So there's a tradeoff.
[06:20] Sahil Rao: Do you have the exact confusion matrix for that?
[06:22] Jamal Ortiz: Yes, it's in the sheet. We'll export a per-template confusion matrix and sample failed outputs.
[06:30] Evan Park: On acceptance criteria — Laura, you had previously said p90 latency under 350ms and quality pass rate above 90% on high-value flows. Is that still accurate?
[06:39] Laura Martinez: Yes, for checkout upsell flows that's the target. For low-value autocomplete we accept 200ms.
[06:45] Maya Chen: Okay we'll mark those as gating criteria for pilot success.
[06:49] Jamal Ortiz: One more note on guardrails — we can run a lightweight local whitelist process that avoids hitting the safety model for allowed catalog phrases; that will reduce the false positives dramatically. It's essentially a pre-check before full safety inference.
[07:02] Sahil Rao: Sounds good. Can you prioritize that for product-recs?
[07:06] Jamal Ortiz: Yes. We'll add it to the engineering queue and include an ETA in the follow-up.
[07:12] Evan Park: Anything else on regressions? Any indication we need model rollback?
[07:16] Jamal Ortiz: Not yet — the regression is fixable via reranking and guardrail tuning. If we still see >5% regression after the next run, we'll discuss a temporary rollback to v2 or a targeted patch.
[07:28] Laura Martinez: Ok, sounds reasonable.
[07:31] Maya Chen: Quick recap and next steps — Maya to send pricing + SOC2 + security questionnaire; Jamal to run extended eval on 10k prompts including the edge-case sets and share confusion matrices; Sahil to deliver prompt sets; Laura to confirm success criteria. We also agreed to consider Dedicated for heavy routes and use routing policies.
[07:53] Evan Park: One more ask: can you also share the runbook for incident responses if a guardrail flags at scale? Our ops team wants the playbook.
[08:01] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll include the incident runbook and the rollback playbook.
[08:05] Laura Martinez: Great, thanks everyone.
[08:08] Maya Chen: Thanks, we'll follow up with the links and the sheet. Bye.
[08:12] (call ends)

Notes: Transcript has occasional ASR misspellings (e.g., "K-V cash" for KV cache), speaker labels are accurate to the best of the auto-transcript. Shared artifacts: https://redwood.link/brightcart-eval-2025 (results sheet), https://redwood.link/brightcart-deck-2025 (proposal deck).
